sections.overview: The sand lizard ranges widely across Europe and into Central Asia.
sections.identification: Males often develop bright green flanks in spring; females are generally browner with rows of dark markings.
sections.habitat: It uses sunny habitats with cover and places to shelter or lay eggs; suitable sites vary across its broad range.
sections.diet: Its prey includes insects and other small invertebrates.
sections.behavior: In Britain, the species is associated especially with sandy heathland and coastal dunes; this is a regional pattern, not a range-wide rule.
sections.reproduction: Females lay eggs in warm, suitable ground; the young hatch after an incubation period that varies with conditions.
sections.ecology: Habitat degradation is identified as a major local threat in the French regional account.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN Red List assessment is Least Concern, assessed in 2018; local populations may face stronger pressures.
